chunks: It is narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said:

Salamah ibn Muḥriz asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام while I was present, and he said: “I performed tawaf of the House and between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah, then I came to Minā and had relations with my wife, and I had not performed Tawaf al-Nisāʾ.” So he said, “What an evil thing you have done.” Then he ascribed ignorance to me, so I said, “I was afflicted with this.” He said, “There is nothing upon you.”

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two places of saʿy
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other place of saʿy
key_terms.بِئْسَ: an expression of censure meaning 'evil' or 'bad'
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: of the House, referring to the Kaʿbah
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa, the tawaf after which marital relations become permitted
key_terms.طُفْتُ: I performed tawaf, meaning ritual circumambulation
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْكَ: there is no penalty or liability upon you
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the hajj site where pilgrims stay during the rites

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone has relations with his wife before performing Tawaf al-Nisa during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a hajj-related legal issue involving marital relations before performing Tawaf al-Nisa. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام condemns the act but ultimately states that no penalty is due in this case, indicating a ruling connected to ignorance or extenuating circumstance.
